title: A young child of anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis presenting with epilepsia partialis continua: the first pediatric case in Korea
case_prompt: A previously healthy 3-year-old girl was brought to the hospital after a 15-minute focal seizure involving the right arm and leg with lip smacking and unresponsiveness, without preceding febrile illness. Perinatal history was notable only for mild motor delay. On initial neurologic exam she was alert with no focal deficits. Brain MRI and EEG were unremarkable. On day 3, she had a recurrent 3-minute partial seizure and was started on oxcarbazepine. On day 5, her seizures evolved into epilepsia partialis continua lasting 80 minutes, halted only after loading phenytoin and phenobarbital. Repeat interictal EEG showed sharp waves over the left frontal region and 1–2-Hz high-amplitude delta activity over the right hemisphere. CSF was not obtained at that time. By week 2, seizures were better controlled but she was transferred for persistent focal seizures and decreased activity. Follow-up EEG demonstrated 4–6-Hz sharply contoured theta waves in the left fronto-central area and 1–2-Hz high-amplitude delta activity in the right parieto-occipital area. Brain MRI now showed a T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesion in the subcortical left posterior parietal lobe. Despite seizure control, she developed sleep disturbance. In week 3, she exhibited prominent oro-lingual-facial dyskinesias, choreoathetoid movements of her limbs, and hypertension (>99th percentile). These movements had no epileptic correlate. EEG revealed diffuse delta activity with superimposed rhythmic beta activity (“extreme delta brush”). Infectious workup was negative, and an autoimmune cause was suspected.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Considered inflammatory or metabolic encephalopathy — “CSF was not tested due to low probability of inflammatory or metabolic encephalopathy.”  
2. Considered infectious encephalitis — “serological or CSF studies for infectious encephalitis ... were all unremarkable.”  
3. Considered paraneoplastic encephalitis — “The patient's serum and CSF studies for paraneoplastic encephalitis (antibodies to Hu, Yo, and Ri) ... were all unremarkable.”  
4. Considered other autoimmune encephalopathies — “possible known autoimmune etiologies that could cause an encephalopathy, including antinuclear antibody, antithyroid antibodies, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies, were all unremarkable.”  
5. Considered inborn errors of metabolism — “inborn errors of metabolism were all unremarkable.”  
6. Considered occult malignancy — “... for malignant tumor ... were all unremarkable.”
